soundness_flags.label: def:model-class; lem:causal-identification; target_estimand
soundness_flags.one_line: P is explicitly an observed-data law on (W,A,Y), but the defining class conditions and the causal equality quantify the undeclared potential-outcome process Y(a); define a full-data law with P as its observed marginal, or define M as observed laws admitting such an extension.

soundness_flags.label: thm:canonical-excursion and its downstream definitions
soundness_flags.one_line: The asserted intensity, centering expansion, admissible block range, declustering rule, mesh, padding, and contact radius are only described as objects 'derived by Theorem 1', so the headline has no independently checkable probability statement or constructive calibration target.

soundness_flags.label: def:model-class; thm:causal-transfer
soundness_flags.one_line: The unrestricted positive constants need compatibility/nonemptiness conditions (including density-integral and bound relations); otherwise M can be empty and the advertised uniform statistical result is vacuous.

source_verification_receipts.version: author PDF dated 20 July 2001; inspected as corroboration because the exact Annals full text was not accessible
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1-3, especially equation (1.2); Theorem 2.5 on p. 12
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies a fixed-point monotone LR test and identifies its universal limit as the integral of the difference of squared constrained and unconstrained Brownian--GCM slope processes.
The cited paper studies extremes of the stationary Brownian-parabolic argmax displacement process and its absolute value on increasing intervals.

source_verification_receipts.version: Probability Theory and Related Fields 78 (1988), publisher primary landing page
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Under dependence conditions, high-level exceedance point-process limits are compound Poisson and yield extreme-order-statistic limits; it does not instantiate those conditions for the LR field.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of Statistics 40(3) (2012), repository record for the published article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives a Gumbel limit for the supremum-norm error of a Grenander-type estimator on an interior subinterval, not for a constrained-versus-unconstrained LR energy field.

The paper proposes causal isotonic regression for a monotone causal dose-response curve, describes irregular limits and doubly robust inference, and does not claim a simultaneous LR extreme-value law.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Publisher abstract and article metadata; corroborated by arXiv:2508.08415 abstract
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article develops doubly robust likelihood-ratio-type confidence intervals for the monotone continuous treatment-effect curve at a fixed point, with cross-fitted and flatness-adaptive versions.
The paper uses a debiased local-linear estimator and empirical-process supremum approximation to construct valid uniform confidence bands for the covariate-adjusted regression function.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the observed-law-only causal model by a full-data extension formulation, state compatibility inequalities ensuring M is nonempty, and then restate every uniform claim over the resulting observed marginals.

Make Theorem 1 independently mathematical: define the truncation radius, mesh and run sequence, Palm-cluster event, lambda(u), its claimed expansion class, and the exact uniform u/ell(u) regime before using them in b(T), a(T), and simulation.

Add a theorem-level comparison showing that the proposed calibration is not merely a simultaneous alternative to existing Gaussian bands—for example, a precise non-equivalence or a regime where the LR profile delivers an identifiable inferential advantage.

recommended_next_step: Revise the model and canonical-excursion statement to remove the two well-posedness/vacuity risks, then retain this field-grade novelty spine for Stage 0.
